## Per-Change Detail

### 1. (critical) Agent orchestration peer-prompt messageID — N/A for Alexi
**Upstream commit:** `d894e6535` + `bf5705bb3`
**Decision:** No code change required.
Alexi does not have an `AgentManagerOrchestrationBridge` / peer-prompt
dispatch surface. The only `promptAsync` / `client.session.prompt`
analogue in Alexi is the in-process `src/session/queue.ts`, whose
`messageID` is always caller-supplied (used for cancel/edit correlation)
and NOT serialized to a backend. There is no backend here that would
assign chronological IDs. Documented explicitly to avoid rework next
sync cycle.

### 2. (high) Ripgrep hardening — invalid pattern + ignore files + exclude
**Upstream commits:** `501286ba9`, `93519a31c`, `21164ba0b`
**Files:** `src/tool/tools/grep.ts`

- Added `GrepResult.invalidPattern?: boolean` so callers can distinguish
  a malformed pattern (don't retry) from a transient `rg` failure
  (eligible for retry).
- Exported `isInvalidRgPattern(stderr)` classifier that matches on
  `regex parse error`, `error parsing regex`, and `error parsing glob`.
- Converted `executeWithRg` to accept an `RgExecuteOptions` object with
  three new fields:
  - `exclude?: readonly string[]` — additional `--glob=!<pattern>`
    exclusions, so a suggestion/marketplace scan can honor caller-
    declared ignored directories (upstream `21164ba0b`).
  - `noRequireGit?: boolean` — pass `--no-require-git` so rg honors
    `.gitignore` / `.ignore` files outside git repos (upstream
    `93519a31c`). When set we drop the hard-coded
    `--no-ignore-vcs` / `--no-ignore-parent` pair so rg's ignore-file
    machinery can actually fire.
  - Positional-arg overload preserved for backward compatibility — the
    `grepTool` call site still passes `(pattern, searchDir, include,
    signal)`.
- `RgSpawnError` thrown on exit code ≥ 2 is now tagged with
  `invalidPattern: true` when the stderr matches `isInvalidRgPattern`.
  The `grepTool` catch block short-circuits that case into
  `{ success: false, error: 'Invalid search pattern: ...' }` instead of
  falling through to the JS walker (which would then fail identically
  on its own regex compile and waste a retry).

### 3. (high) Catalog recovery retry with Retry-After honoring
**Upstream commits:** `07b18a1a2`, `b1642e87c`, `88f8ea950`, `59313c749`,
`5539dd3ae`
**Files:** `src/providers/catalog-retry.ts` (new),
`src/providers/__tests__/catalog-retry.test.ts` (new),
`src/providers/modelCatalog.ts` (barrel re-export)

- New module exports:
  - `parseRetryAfter(header)` — RFC 7231 §7.1.3 support for both
    delta-seconds and HTTP-date forms; clamps past dates to `0`;
    returns `undefined` for garbage.
  - `withCatalogRetry(fn, opts?, signal?)` — bounded exponential-backoff
    retry loop that prefers `retryAfterMs` from a 429/503 over the
    exponential schedule, honors `signal.aborted` BEFORE every attempt
    and during the backoff sleep, and throws the last error after
    exhaustion. Each top-level call starts with a fresh counter —
    satisfies the "rearm after success" clause from upstream.
  - `DEFAULT_CATALOG_RETRY` — matches `src/core/error-backoff.ts`
    constants (5 attempts, 1s base, 30s cap).
- Did NOT replace the existing `fetchWithRetry` in
  `modelFetchErrors.ts` — that helper is bonded to the SAP SDK's
  thrown-error shape. `withCatalogRetry` is a Result-returning sibling
  for new HTTP-based catalog fetches that need to inspect response
  headers. Both are re-exported from `modelCatalog.ts` so callers
  pick the right one based on which transport they're on.
- 7 unit tests cover parsing, success-on-first-try, retry-until-success,
  exhaustion, Retry-After vs exponential, abort before attempt,
  invalid options, and the rearm-after-success contract.

### 4. (high) Provider model cache resilience to a single malformed entry
**Upstream commit:** `2792c704e`
**Files:** `src/providers/modelCatalog.ts`

- Wrapped `extractModelId(d.configurationName)` in a per-deployment
  `try/catch` inside `refreshModelCatalog`. A thrown parse error (bad
  shape, non-string `configurationName`, future schema addition that
  Alexi's static heuristics don't understand) is now logged at `debug`
  and the loop CONTINUES. Previously the throw would propagate up to
  the outer catch, flip the catalog into `error` state, and leave the
  user with only the static seed — even though 99% of the live
  deployment list was perfectly valid.
- When at least one entry was skipped, we emit a single warn-level
  summary (`skipped N malformed entry/ies; kept M valid model(s)`) so
  the operator can see WHY their deployment count doesn't match the
  SAP cockpit without having to crank up the log verbosity.
- `extractModelId` itself is still a pure, defensive helper — nothing
  about this change requires it to throw. The guard is in place so a
  future refactor (or an upstream SDK shape change) can't silently
  break the whole catalog.

### 5. (medium) Skill frontmatter cache
**Upstream commit:** `b0aeda50b`
**Files:** `src/skill/index.ts`, `src/skill/frontmatter-cache.test.ts`
(new)

- Added a module-local `Map<resolvedPath, { skill, size, mtimeMs }>` and
  wired it into `loadSkillFromFile`. Before parsing the file we
  `fs.statSync` to grab `(size, mtimeMs)`; if both match a cached
  entry, we return the cached `Skill` without re-reading or
  re-parsing. On any stat failure we fall through to a fresh parse
  (never serve a stale read without an invalidation key).
- After a successful parse, the fresh Skill is written into the cache
  keyed by the earlier stat values. A subsequent edit to the skill
  file bumps the mtime, which invalidates the entry on the next
  `loadSkillFromFile`.
- Exposed `_resetSkillFrontmatterCacheForTests` as the internal escape
  hatch for unit tests (matches the project convention — see
  `_resetRgDetectionForTests` in `grep.ts`).
- Tests verify (a) reference equality on repeated loads of an
  unchanged file (proof of cache hit) and (b) a mtime bump produces a
  fresh Skill with the new description.

## Issues Encountered

- The plan was truncated at change 4 mid-sentence. Changes 5–7 were
  reconstructed from the summary table and the upstream commit list.
- Alexi's architecture diverges meaningfully from kilocode on three
  surfaces (ripgrep wrapper lives in the `grep` tool, not a core
  module; peer-prompt dispatch doesn't exist; catalog uses the SAP SDK
  rather than raw `fetch()`), so some proposed changes were adapted
  to the actual code shape rather than applied verbatim. Every
  adaptation is called out in the per-change notes above with the
  upstream commit hash it ports.
